subject: Request: Final-mile delivery SLA exception for nightly batch inference
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.example.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Safety <bob.safety@acme.example.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final-mile delivery SLA: nightly batch completion variability

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. We run a large nightly aggregation pipeline against Redwood dedicated endpoints that kicks off ~1.8M items at 02:00 UTC and usually completes within our contractual finalization window (3:00–03:30 UTC), but over the last 6 weeks we've seen a long-tail where 0.8–1.2% of jobs are finishing well past the window (sometimes into the 04:30 UTC hour). We've attached a short sample of logs showing the tail behavior.

This is starting to block downstream reporting and raises questions with our compliance team about data availability. We're asking whether Redwood can provide a formal, time-bound SLA exception for the "final-mile" of nightly batch runs while we implement idempotent retry logic on our side. Specifically: 

- Can Redwood grant a 90-minute soft-grace period for nightly finalization for the next 90 days?
- What retry semantics will Redwood guarantee if we safely retry failed tasks (at-least-once vs exactly-once expectations)?
- Any recommended idempotency key patterns or best practices so we avoid double-processing when retries occur?

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the logs. Our compliance/ops lead Bob is cc'd.

Thanks,
Alice
Senior Data Platform Engineer
Acme Data

Attachments: acme_nightly_error_sample.log (text), sla_history.csv (csv)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Bob Safety <bob.safety@acme.example.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final-mile delivery SLA: nightly batch completion variability

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the clear summary and the logs — helpful. Short answers up front: we can put a temporary, documented grace window in place while we work through mitigations, and we have guidance for safe retrying + idempotency. That said, to finalize this we need a tiny bit more detail and to align commercial terms (credit vs adjusted SLO).

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood proposes a temporary 90-minute nightly "final-mile" grace window for the next 90 days (we'll record this as an SLO amendment).
- Technical: we'll provide a recommended idempotency pattern + retry backoff table. See attached draft matrix (retry-idempotency-matrix.xlsx).
- Ops: schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk logs and confirm expected tail behavior and the success criteria for removing the exception.

Questions for you:
1) Can you share the per-run item throughput distribution (P50/P95/P99) and whether those late completions are concentrated on specific model variants?
2) Are you ok with an "at-least-once" default retry behavior from Redwood if you implement idempotent keys, with a documented mitigation path for any accidental duplicates?

I've looped in Ben for the commercial side and Grace for SRE/observability; we'll take notes in the HubSpot deal.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: retry-idempotency-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.example.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Bob Safety <bob.safety@acme.example.com>
Date: Sat, 3 May 2025 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final-mile delivery SLA: nightly batch completion variability

Hi Alice — quick commercial note from my side.

We can do the 90-minute final-mile grace window for a 90-day pilot with the following guardrails:
- Grace window applies only to scheduled nightly jobs between 00:00–06:00 UTC.
- If >1% of nightly jobs breach the standard finalization window for 3 consecutive nights, we will trigger the remediation runbook and offer a 10% usage credit for the impacted nightly runs that exceed the baseline threshold.
- After the 90-day pilot we'll either revert to standard SLA, extend the exception, or convert it to a permanent SLO amendment depending on telemetry and agreed success criteria.

If that's acceptable from Acme's side, I'll draft the SLA amendment PDF and route for electronic signature. Neha / Grace — please add any technical caveats (idempotency, safe retry windows, maximum retry attempts).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: sla_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Safety <bob.safety@acme.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 08:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final-mile delivery SLA: nightly batch completion variability

Hi Ben / Neha,

Thanks — the proposed pilot terms look reasonable. A couple of technical clarifications before we sign: 

- Idempotency: we will implement idempotency keys at the item level, but we need Redwood to guarantee a no-double-processing clause for any retries initiated by our system within the first 30 minutes after failure (i.e., if we retry a payload with the same idempotency key within that window, Redwood should ensure it is not processed twice).
- Retry cap: we prefer a maximum of 3 retry attempts with exponential backoff starting at 15s.
- Observability: we need nightly reports showing the count of late completions, their model variants, and the retry vs fresh-processing breakdown. Can Redwood provide a dashboard URL or nightly CSV export?

If you can confirm those three points, we can mark this approved on our side and proceed with the 90-day pilot.

Best,
Alice

On Mon, 5 May 2025 at 07:22 Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alice — quick note ahead of our call: we can meet all three asks with the following clarifications:
> - No-double-processing: Redwood will honor idempotency keys for the configured retry window (default 60 minutes for the pilot); behavior equals "exactly-once" for retries with the same key during that window. Any duplicate beyond the window is considered a new request.
> - Retry cap: we'll implement configurable server-side caps; for the pilot we'll set server-side max=3 with exponential backoff (15s, 60s, 240s).
> - Observability: Grace will provision a nightly CSV export and a per-run dashboard for the pilot (shared link).
>
> Neha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acme.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Bob Safety <bob.safety@acme.example.com>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final-mile delivery SLA: nightly batch completion variability

Alice / team —

Confirming in writing what we discussed and agreed on the call:

- Pilot: 90-day final-mile grace window (90 minutes) for nightly scheduled jobs (00:00–06:00 UTC).
- Idempotency/Retry: Redwood will honor idempotency keys for retries within a 60-minute server-side window for the pilot (effectively preventing double-processing within that window). Server-side caps: 3 retries, exponential backoff (15s, 60s, 240s).
- Observability: nightly CSV export + dashboard link will be available; Grace will share the dashboard invite and export schedule by EOD tomorrow.
- Commercial: if >1% of nightly jobs breach the standard window for 3 consecutive nights, Acme will be eligible for a 10% usage credit for impacted runs (as described in sla_proposal_v2.pdf).

Next actions:
1) Ben to route SLA amendment for electronic signature (Ben: target Wed EOD).
2) Grace to share dashboard and nightly export schedule.
3) Acme to implement idempotency keys and share P50/P95/P99 throughput details.

Thanks and looking forward to the pilot.

-Neha

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184
